tasks.short: Turn pay, benefits and grading research into reports, manuals and explainers for staff, management and the works council.

steps.what: Pull pay, grade and benefits figures from AFAS extract into Excel tables and charts
Write the narrative: findings, method, plain-language explanation per job group

loop.input: Fixed figures table, last year's report, report template with section headings
loop.output: Draft text per section with each number referenced to a table cell
loop.check: Script compares every number in the text to the figures table; mismatches are flagged; specialist edits and signs off
loop.stop: One draft per section, up to two regenerations; after that the specialist writes the section
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining why figures moved and wording it for warehouse staff is free text that a template alone cannot produce

steps.what: Check figures and remove groups small enough to identify a person
Review with HR Director and discuss with the works council where needed
Lay out in house style and publish on SharePoint or send out

tasks.design: A small Python job on the governed data platform reads the nightly AFAS extract and produces the figure tables and charts, with groups under a set size suppressed. It fills a Word template on SharePoint, and a bounded model step drafts the narrative per section; a script checks every number against the table. The specialist edits, the HR Director approves, and publishing is a SharePoint page or PDF from the same template.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work happens once a year or less, so nobody built a pipeline. Figures were rebuilt by hand in Excel each time.
tasks.enabler_now: The pay transparency law adds a yearly report (first over 2027 pay, due 7 June 2028), which turns a one-off into a recurring job. AI coding makes a small report pipeline cheap, and model drafting is good enough for a first version that a person edits.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining pay differences honestly and choosing what to publish. Small groups at three sites make anonymisation tricky, and the CAO regrading outcome is still open.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the numbers mean, what Noordhaven is willing to say in public, and how the works council will read it.

ambition.what: A one-page pay scale and benefits explainer per job group for warehouse and transport shift workers, in Dutch and Polish, refreshed from the same pipeline each year.

tasks.altitude: About 10 of the 16 hours a year go; the specialist spends the rest on interpreting the figures and on the works council discussion. Nothing changes in decision rights.

reach.task: Maintain the Power BI pay dashboards on the AFAS extract
reach.learn: How the extract defines job groups and headcount, so report figures match the dashboards.

reach.task: Explain pay and grading questions to managers
reach.learn: Which questions come up most, so the explainer answers them first.

evidence.claim: Noordhaven must report pay gaps yearly, first over 2027 pay by 7 June 2028; agency workers count.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency.
49% of employers say salary structures lag job changes, which makes explaining them harder.
A model can draft report text from a fixed table if a script checks the numbers afterwards.

assumptions: The research published is mostly internal: pay reports, benefits manuals, a pay transparency report, not academic journals.
A governed data platform or at least a scheduled script host is available next to the AFAS extract.
The Word template and SharePoint site already exist.
unknowns: Which publications the specialist actually produces each year and for whom.
Whether the works council wants to see draft reports before management.
The minimum group size Noordhaven uses for publishing pay figures.
research_questions: How many hours did the last pay or benefits report take, and how much was figure work versus writing?
Do the AFAS job schemes map cleanly to the four-factor job groups needed for the transparency report?
Does the works council accept model-drafted text if the specialist signs off on it?
Would shift workers read a one-page explainer, and in which languages?

role.altitude: From building pay figures and documents by hand to owning the job architecture and the evidence behind every pay difference, ready for the 2028 transparency report.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: the AFAS extract and job group definitions
Payroll Specialist: CAO costing and pay cycle data
HR Business Partner: manager questions on pay and grading
Works council liaison via the HR Director
skills_to_grow: Reading and checking a scripted data pipeline
Reviewing model drafts against source figures
Explaining pay to shift workers in plain language
role.ambitious_version: One pipeline from AFAS produces the yearly gap report, per-group pay explainers and answers to individual pay requests within two months, with every unexplained gap flagged early and taken to the works council before the six-month deadline.
